intro: Thailand is the only country in Southeast Asia that was never colonised by a European power. Its kingdoms grew from Sukhothai to Ayutthaya to today's Bangkok.

chapters.title: Early kingdoms
text: Thai-speaking peoples moved south from what is now southern China over many centuries. In the 1200s they founded the kingdom of Sukhothai, whose name means 'dawn of happiness'. King Ramkhamhaeng is said to have created the Thai alphabet.
Before that, much of the region was ruled by the Mon and by the Khmer Empire of Angkor.

chapters.title: Ayutthaya
text: From 1351 Ayutthaya became one of the richest cities in Asia, trading with China, Japan, Persia and Europe. Visitors compared it to Paris and London.

In 1767 Burmese armies destroyed the city. General Taksin drove them out and founded a new capital, and in 1782 the Chakri dynasty moved it across the river to Bangkok, where the same royal family still reigns.

highlight.title: Ruins today
highlight.text: Ayutthaya's ruined temples, with a Buddha head wrapped in tree roots, are a World Heritage site.

chapters.title: Never colonised
text: In the 1800s Britain and France took control of all Siam's neighbours. Kings Mongkut and Chulalongkorn modernised the country, built railways and gave up some territory to stay independent.
In 1932 a revolution ended absolute monarchy, and in 1939 Siam was renamed Thailand. Since then the army has seized power many times, most recently in 2006 and 2014.

timeline.title: Ayutthaya
timeline.text: A great trading city is founded.

timeline.title: Tsunami
timeline.text: Thousands die on the Andaman coast.
